claim: A completed sale can be recorded as a dismissal, and 1 of our 3 production sales is. PostHog purchase counts are a lower bound; RevenueCat is the source of truth for money.

body.decision: DEC-282 (2026-08-13). Re-verified against the mirror at HEAD f20a064.
body.what: A completed sale can be recorded as a dismissal. 1 of our 3 production sales is recorded that way in PostHog right now.
body.mechanism: paywall_screen.dart:213 awaits service.purchasePackage(...), line 217 then does 'if (!mounted) return;'. The await runs up to 8s inside waitForEntitlement (entitlement_service.dart:470) against a 10s call timeout. Dispose in that window and neither capturePurchaseSucceeded nor _fireResult runs, so dispose() at line 89 fires 'dismissed' because _resultFired is still false.
body.second_path: case PurchaseOutcome.cancelled: break; at line 251 fires nothing at all, so a genuine cancel and a dropped sale are indistinguishable.
body.evidence: The Pakistan buyer's paywall_result outcome=dismissed is stamped 23:09:37, the same second RevenueCat recorded the receipt.
body.ticket: DAL-237, retitled from "instrument paywall views" (work already done) to the defect, description rewritten, Todo, assigned to Benedict.
body.fix_part_1: Fire the purchase events from inside EntitlementService.purchasePackage rather than the widget callback, and give cancelled its own outcome value. Small, no privacy implications, Benedict commits it.
body.fix_part_2: Push the PostHog distinct id to RevenueCat as a subscriber attribute at configure time so anonymous buyers are attributable. Benedict's privacy call, deliberately separate.
body.consequence: Every paywall dismissal rate we have quoted is an upper bound, and PostHog purchase counts are a lower bound. RevenueCat remains the source of truth for money.
